key_insight: Neural scaling laws extend to weather emulation: using a minimal Swin Transformer and a continual-training protocol, performance scales predictably with model size, data, and compute—allowing reliable extrapolation of gains from increased scale.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of quantitative understanding about how model, data, and compute scaling (and continual training on streaming data) affect performance for weather forecasting/emulation in Scientific ML.
method: Adopt a minimal, scalable Swin Transformer as a general-purpose weather emulator to keep architectural confounders low.
Run controlled scaling experiments that sweep model size, dataset size, and compute to characterize empirical scaling laws.
Use a continual-training protocol that simulates streaming weather data to measure long-term performance, transfer, and data efficiency.
impact: Gives practitioners a practical framework to predict returns from scaling and to allocate model/data/compute budgets for weather emulators; informs design of efficient continual-training strategies for Earth-system foundation models.
visual_elements: Log–log plots of validation loss / forecast skill vs model size, dataset size, and compute showing scaling (power-law) trends.
Schematic diagram of the minimal Swin Transformer architecture used (patches, attention windows) to emphasize simplicity and scalability.
Timeline visualization of continual training: streaming data segments with a performance curve showing adaptation and cumulative gains.
Geospatial heatmap comparing forecast error across lead times and model scales to illustrate practical impact on predictions.
paper_title: On Neural Scaling Laws for Weather Emulation through Continual Training
paper_authors: Shashank Subramanian, Alexander Kiefer, Arnur Nigmetov, Amir Gholami, Dmitriy Morozov
